bottleneck: Natural exposure to wild-type AAVs leaves 30-70% of people carrying neutralizing antibodies that destroy therapeutic vectors before they reach target cells, with prevalence varying by serotype, region, and age. These long-lasting memory responses blunt or fully block the therapeutic effect, and re-exposure after dosing makes cellular immune responses clear transduced cells, eroding durability. No reliable, general method yet exists to evade or deplete this immunity.
current_state: Screening simply excludes antibody-positive patients from trials and treatment. Capsid engineering and immune-depletion protocols are under active research but remain unproven at scale.

title: Pre-existing immunity to AAV excludes most patients
why_it_blocks: A therapy that works only for a subset of the population cannot be a general medicine. Pre-existing immunity plus post-dose immunity makes AAV effectively a one-shot, one-fraction-of-patients platform, capping both clinical impact and commercial viability.
